scenes.title: Citation Map
scenes.brief: A horizontal timeline from 1900 to 1994 with one dot per reference (123 dots), stacked by year. Dot color = topic family: blue kinematics & screws, teal grasping & contact, purple nonholonomic systems, orange control & dynamics, gold differential geometry & Lie theory, slate hardware & micro-robots. A second layer draws thin threads from each dot to the chapter cards (1–9, A, B) that cite it; hovering a chapter card lights its sources and shows a year histogram. Clicking a dot zooms to the atlas scenes whose atoms cite that number (e.g. [88] → the exp/log scene, [63] → the no-fair-ruler scene). No titles on canvas: only numbers, years and colors.

pages.summary: Bibliography entries 1–14: kinematics and control texts, classical screw theory, contact sensing, nonholonomic stabilization, differential geometry, and the origin of the product-of-exponentials formula.

atoms.idea: Bibliography heading.
Entries 1–6: kinematics and robot-control textbooks (1980s), nonlinear optimal control and redundancy resolution, and a classic treatise on screws from 1900.
Entries 7–9: contact sensing from force measurements, control of nonholonomic dynamic systems, and a standard differential-manifolds textbook.

Entries 10–14: theoretical kinematics, control and sub-Riemannian geometry, the 1984 product-of-exponentials paper, an applied-math robotics symposium volume, and elliptic functions in nonholonomic control.
Page 441

pages.summary: Entries 15–31: geometric chain dynamics, micro-rovers, Jacobian-transpose inverse kinematics, artificial hands, teleoperated force sensing, grasping, redundancy, the 1955 link-parameter notation, and micro-actuators.

atoms.idea: Entries 15–17: geometric dynamics of kinematic chains, a robot-on-a-chip proposal, and closed-loop Jacobian-transpose inverse kinematics.
Entries 18–21: early artificial hand mechanisms, cable-driven teleoperated manipulators with force sensing, a multivolume robot-technology series, and an introductory robotics text.

Entries 22–26: grasping and fine manipulation, gradient methods for redundancy, multifinger planar manipulation experiments, the 1955 matrix notation for lower-pair linkages, and biomechanical finger design.
Entries 27–31: curves-and-surfaces geometry, mechanism and manipulator analysis, mechanism design, and sub-millimeter micro-actuators.
Page 442

pages.summary: Entries 32–49: space-platform attitude control by internal motion, nonholonomic planning, control and robotics texts, nilpotent Lie algebras, group theory, compliant hands, controllability, and nonlinear systems.

atoms.idea: Entries 32–35: attitude control and near-optimal planning for coupled rigid bodies, a feedback-control textbook, and a robotics control/sensing/vision text.

Entries 36–41: manipulator modeling (in French), free nilpotent Lie algebras, group theory, an elastic-finger hand for assembly, nonlinear controllability and observability, and motor-redundancy studies.

Entries 42–49: kinematic geometry of mechanisms, nonlinear control systems, a dextrous-hand progress report, spatial-operator multibody dynamics, computational geometry lectures, compliant quasi-static manipulation, a multifingered-hand thesis, and a nonlinear-systems text.
Page 443

pages.summary: Entries 50–67: operational-space control, natural motion, exact linearization, geometric motion planning, nonholonomic mobile robots, dextrous hands, rolling contact, compliant mechanisms on Lie groups, 6R inverse kinematics, and mechanics.

atoms.idea: Entries 50–54: unified motion/force (operational-space) control, natural arm motion, control fundamentals, exact linearization, and differential-geometric motion planning.
Entries 55–58: smooth collision-free paths for a nonholonomic robot, elliptic functions, a vector theory of mechanisms, and a dextrous-hand thesis.

Entries 59–63: geometric aspects of robot kinematics, rolling contact between rigid bodies, a nonholonomic-planning collection, coordinated multifinger manipulation, and a thesis on compliant mechanisms via Lie groups (source of Appendix A §3).
Entries 64–67: real-time 6R inverse kinematics, an arm with sixteen inverse solutions, grasping geometry, and lectures on mechanics.
Page 444

pages.summary: Entries 68–83: symmetry reduction and phases, hand mechanics, theoretical kinematics, positive grips, contact kinematics, nilpotent bases, control primitives, grasping experiments, steering with sinusoids, redundancy, and force-closure.

atoms.idea: Entries 68–73: reduction and geometric phases in mechanics, robot-hand mechanics, theoretical kinematics, existence of positive multifinger grips, and kinematics of contact (with and without compliance).
Entries 74–78: nilpotent bases for trajectory generation, control primitives, planar grasping experiments, multifingered grasping and manipulation, and steering nonholonomic systems with sinusoids.
Entries 79–83: redundancy and optimization, coordinating multiple mechanisms, nonholonomic dynamics, constructing force-closure grasps, and nonlinear control theory.
Page 445

pages.summary: Entries 84–100: finger control, optimal 6R design, Lie-group dynamics, product-of-exponentials computation, analytical dynamics, micro-hinges and air-bearing actuators, linkage equations, 6R inverse kinematics, convex analysis, spatial operators, and manipulator design.

atoms.idea: Entries 84–90: multijointed finger control, a kinematics-and-control thesis, optimal kinematic design of 6R arms, a Lie-group formulation of dynamics, computational aspects of the product of exponentials, analytical dynamics, and a classic manipulator text.
Entries 91–94: hinged polysilicon micro-structures, a planar air-bearing electrostatic actuator, micro-fabricated hinges, and the input-output equation of a general 7R linkage.

Entries 95–100: a survey of manipulator kinematics, inverse kinematics of the general 6R arm, convex analysis, spatial-operator algebra, analytical dynamics, and early design of computer-controlled manipulators (1973).
Page 446

pages.summary: Entries 101–118: articulated hands, adaptive control, optimal steering, Lie algebras, redundant repeatability, prehension design, differential geometry, robot dynamics and control, the six-DOF platform, trailers, early adaptive hands, sheep-shearing robots, representations, and distributions.

atoms.idea: Entries 101–107: kinematic and force analysis of articulated hands, adaptive control, optimal steering control, Lie algebras and groups, repeatability of redundant arms, multiple-prehension design, and adaptive manipulator control.

Entries 108–113: a comprehensive differential-geometry treatise, a robot-control collection, a dynamics-and-control text, the 1960s six-DOF platform, N-trailer trajectory generation, and a 1962 adaptive artificial hand.
Entries 114–118: robots for shearing sheep, Lie groups and representations, a dextrous-hands collection, nonholonomic problems and distributions, and nonlinear systems analysis.
Page 447

pages.summary: Entries 119–123: reorienting linked bodies by internal motion, manipulator control laws, a symbolic-math system, robotics foundations, and calculus of variations.

atoms.idea: Entries 119–123: reorienting linked rigid bodies by internal motions, new manipulator control laws, the symbolic-math system used in Appendix B, a robotics-foundations text, and calculus of variations and optimal control.
